questions.stem: According to the World Health Organization, health is a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being and not merely the
options: ability to do hard work daily
eating of three meals a day
questions.explanation: This is the WHO definition of health.

questions.topic: Meaning and Setting for Health Education
questions.stem: Health education given to pupils through classroom lessons takes place in the
questions.explanation: Settings include school, home, community, hospital and workplace.

questions.topic: Cells and Tissues of the Human Body
questions.stem: The basic structural and functional unit of the human body is the
questions.explanation: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs and organs form systems.

questions.topic: Cells and Tissues of the Human Body
questions.stem: The organelle often called the powerhouse of the cell because it releases energy is the
questions.explanation: Mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration to release energy.

questions.stem: The receptor cells in the retina that work best in dim light are the
questions.explanation: Rods function in dim light; cones detect colour in bright light.

questions.stem: A long-sighted person who cannot see near objects clearly is corrected with
questions.explanation: Hypermetropia is corrected with converging (convex) lenses.

questions.stem: The longest bone in the human body is the
questions.explanation: The thigh bone (femur) is the longest bone.

questions.stem: The tough fibrous cords that attach muscles to bones are
questions.explanation: Tendons join muscle to bone; ligaments join bone to bone.

questions.stem: Which chamber of the heart has the thickest muscular wall?
questions.explanation: The left ventricle pumps blood round the whole body.

questions.stem: Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood?
questions.explanation: The pulmonary vein brings oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart.

questions.stem: A person with blood group O can donate blood to people of all groups because the red cells carry
questions.explanation: Group O red cells lack A and B antigens.

questions.stem: The enzyme in saliva acts on
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase begins starch digestion.

questions.explanation: The lungs excrete CO2 and water vapour.

questions.stem: Urea is formed in the
questions.explanation: The liver deaminates excess amino acids to form urea, which the kidney removes.

questions.explanation: Alveoli provide the gas-exchange surface.

questions.stem: The central nervous system consists of the
questions.explanation: The CNS is the brain and spinal cord.

questions.stem: The part of the brain that controls breathing and heartbeat is the
questions.explanation: The medulla controls vital involuntary activities.

questions.stem: The gland often called the master gland is the
questions.explanation: The pituitary controls many other endocrine glands.

questions.stem: The hormone that prepares the body for 'fight or flight' is
questions.explanation: Adrenaline from the adrenal glands raises heart rate and blood sugar in emergencies.

questions.stem: The maintenance of a fairly constant internal environment in the body is
questions.explanation: Homeostasis keeps temperature, water and sugar levels stable.

questions.stem: An exaggerated inward curve of the lower back is called
questions.explanation: Lordosis (sway back) affects the lumbar region; kyphosis is a hunched upper back.

questions.stem: Carrying a heavy school bag always on one shoulder may lead to
questions.explanation: Uneven loading can encourage sideways curvature of the spine.

questions.stem: Regular bathing helps to prevent
questions.explanation: Washing removes sweat, dirt and germs from the skin.

questions.stem: Regular physical exercise helps to
questions.explanation: Exercise improves cardiovascular fitness, muscle tone and bone density.

The instrument used to measure blood pressure is the
questions.explanation: A sphygmomanometer (with stethoscope) measures blood pressure.

questions.stem: Fluoride is added to toothpaste mainly to
questions.explanation: Fluoride makes enamel more resistant to acid attack.

questions.stem: Inflammation of the gums, with redness and bleeding when brushing, is
questions.explanation: Gingivitis is gum inflammation, usually from plaque.

questions.stem: Teaching hospitals and federal medical centres provide
questions.explanation: Tertiary care is specialised care at the highest level.

questions.stem: Medical inspection of pupils on admission to school forms part of
questions.explanation: Health appraisal and inspection are school health services.

questions.stem: BCG vaccine, given to babies at birth, protects against
questions.explanation: BCG protects against tuberculosis.

questions.stem: In a district, 300 infants died before their first birthday in a year with 6,000 live births. The infant mortality rate is
A bereaved person who refuses to believe that a loved one has died is in the stage of grief known as
questions.explanation: Denial is usually the first reaction to loss.

questions.stem: The number of new cases of a disease occurring in a population over a given period is its
questions.explanation: Incidence counts new cases; prevalence counts all existing cases.

questions.stem: A disease that is constantly present at a low level in a particular area, such as malaria in Nigeria, is
questions.explanation: Endemic diseases are habitually present in an area.

questions.stem: Overcrowding in a poorly ventilated room most readily favours the spread of
questions.explanation: Airborne infections such as TB and CSM spread easily in crowded rooms.

questions.stem: A layer of impermeable material placed in the walls of a building near ground level to stop rising moisture is the
questions.explanation: The damp-proof course prevents damp from rising into walls.

questions.stem: Drinking water from an unprotected stream is most likely to cause
questions.explanation: Contaminated water spreads typhoid, cholera and dysentery.

questions.stem: Guinea worm infection is contracted by drinking water containing infected
questions.explanation: Cyclops carry guinea-worm larvae; filtering water prevents infection.

questions.stem: Turning kitchen and garden waste into manure is called
questions.explanation: Composting decomposes organic waste into manure.

questions.stem: A ventilated improved pit (VIP) latrine reduces flies and odour by means of a
options: vent pipe with a fly screen
questions.explanation: The screened vent pipe draws out odours and traps flies.

questions.stem: Gas flaring in the Niger Delta mainly causes
questions.explanation: Flaring releases smoke, soot and gases into the air.

questions.stem: Acid rain is formed mainly when rainwater dissolves
questions.explanation: SO2 and NOx dissolve in rain to form acids.

questions.stem: Workers in a battery recycling factory are most at risk of
questions.explanation: Lead from batteries can poison workers.

questions.stem: Ear muffs, goggles and helmets provided to factory workers are examples of
questions.explanation: PPE protects workers from occupational hazards.

questions.stem: Lassa fever is spread mainly by
questions.explanation: The multimammate rat (Mastomys natalensis) is the reservoir of Lassa virus.

questions.stem: Sleeping sickness is transmitted by the
questions.explanation: Tsetse flies transmit trypanosomes.

questions.stem: Lack of protein in a child's diet can lead to
questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor results from protein deficiency.

questions.topic: Factors Influencing Feeding Habits and Choice of Foods
questions.stem: A Muslim who does not eat pork is influenced in food choice mainly by
questions.explanation: Religious beliefs shape food habits.

questions.stem: Water makes up about what proportion of an adult's body weight?
questions.explanation: Water forms roughly 60-70 per cent of body weight.

questions.stem: The movement of digested food from the small intestine into the blood is
questions.explanation: Absorption occurs through the villi of the small intestine.

questions.topic: Diet for Different Groups of People
questions.stem: A lactating mother needs extra fluids and calcium mainly to
questions.explanation: Milk production requires more water, calcium and energy.

questions.stem: An unconscious casualty who is breathing normally should be placed in the
options: face-up position with head raised high
questions.explanation: The recovery position keeps the airway open.

questions.stem: In adult cardiopulmonary resuscitation, the recommended ratio of chest compressions to rescue breaths is
questions.explanation: Current guidelines recommend 30 compressions to 2 breaths.

questions.stem: Before touching a person receiving an electric shock, the first aider should
options: pull the person with bare hands
questions.explanation: Breaking contact with the current protects the rescuer.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a man-made disaster?
questions.explanation: Building collapse results from human error or negligence.

questions.stem: The agency responsible for road safety and traffic management on Nigerian highways is the
options: Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps
questions.explanation: The FRSC manages road safety.

questions.stem: Training a person who has lost a leg to walk again with an artificial limb is
questions.explanation: Rehabilitation restores function and independence.

questions.stem: When a person needs more and more of a drug to get the same effect, the person has developed
questions.explanation: Tolerance means a larger dose is needed for the same effect.

questions.stem: Cocaine and amphetamines are classified as
questions.explanation: They speed up nervous system activity.

questions.stem: Sniffing glue, petrol or other solvents to get 'high' is abuse of
questions.explanation: Volatile solvents are inhalants and can damage the brain.

questions.stem: A disease caused by a micro-organism that can spread from person to person is
questions.explanation: Infectious (communicable) diseases are caused by pathogens.

questions.stem: Tetanus germs usually enter the body through
questions.explanation: Clostridium tetani spores enter deep, dirty wounds.

questions.stem: HIV weakens the immune system by destroying
questions.explanation: HIV infects CD4 T-helper cells.

questions.stem: A blood pressure reading consistently above 140/90 mmHg in an adult indicates
questions.explanation: Persistently raised pressure is hypertension.

questions.stem: The male reproductive cells (sperm) are produced in the
questions.explanation: Sperm are made in the testes.

questions.stem: The stage of life at which the reproductive organs mature and secondary sexual characteristics appear is
questions.explanation: Puberty brings sexual maturity and changes such as breast development and voice deepening.

questions.stem: Providing guidance, love and discipline to children is mainly the role of
questions.explanation: Parents nurture, guide and discipline their children.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common challenge to stable family life?
questions.explanation: Poor communication often leads to conflict and breakdown.

questions.stem: Which family planning method is permanent for a man?
questions.explanation: Vasectomy cuts and ties the sperm ducts; tubal ligation is the female equivalent.

questions.stem: A country has a crude birth rate of 38 per 1,000 and a crude death rate of 12 per 1,000. Its rate of natural increase is
A persistent, irrational fear of a particular object or situation, such as heights, is a
questions.explanation: A phobia is an intense, unreasonable fear.

questions.topic: Attributes of Emotional and Social Health
questions.stem: A student who can control anger and express feelings appropriately shows good
questions.explanation: Emotional health includes managing feelings well.

questions.topic: Interrelationship of Emotional and Social Health
questions.stem: A student who is constantly anxious and withdrawn is likely to find it difficult to
questions.explanation: Poor emotional health often harms social relationships.

options: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
questions.explanation: The PCN regulates pharmacy practice.

questions.topic: Factors Influencing Choice of Consumer Products
questions.stem: A teenager buys a skin cream because a popular musician praised it on television. The factor influencing the choice is
questions.explanation: Advertising strongly influences consumer choices.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a consumer health service rather than a health product?
questions.explanation: Services are activities provided by professionals; products are goods bought and used.

questions.stem: A patient who wants a second opinion on a diagnosis should consult
options: a herbal advertiser on the radio
a friend who has had similar symptoms
questions.explanation: Second opinions should come from qualified, registered practitioners.

questions.topic: Health Insurance and Advertisement of Health Products and Services
questions.stem: An advertisement claiming that a single herbal tea cures diabetes, cancer and HIV should be regarded as
questions.explanation: Claims to cure many unrelated serious diseases are a sign of false advertising.

questions.stem: The main danger of using a nostrum is that it
options: may delay proper treatment of a serious illness
questions.explanation: Nostrums have secret ingredients and unproven claims, so they may harm or delay effective care.

questions.stem:
(a) Name the three types of blood vessels. [3 marks]
(b) State one difference between an artery and a vein. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Arteries
1 mark: Veins
1 mark: Capillaries
2 marks: Arteries carry blood away from the heart with thick elastic walls; veins carry blood to the heart, have thinner walls and valves
questions.explanation: The vessels are arteries, veins and capillaries. Arteries carry blood away from the heart under high pressure and have thick walls; veins return blood to the heart and have valves.

questions.stem:
(a) State three practices that promote healthy teeth. [3 marks]
(b) Name two dental diseases. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Brushing twice daily with fluoride toothpaste
1 mark: Reducing sugary snacks and drinks
1 mark: Regular dental check-ups or flossing
1 mark: Dental caries
1 mark: Gingivitis or periodontal disease
questions.explanation: Brush twice daily with fluoride paste, limit sugar and visit the dentist. Common diseases are dental caries and gum disease.

questions.stem:
(a) Name the vector of each of the following diseases: (i) yellow fever (ii) sleeping sickness. [2 marks]
(b) State three ways of controlling houseflies. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Yellow fever: Aedes mosquito
1 mark: Sleeping sickness: tsetse fly
1 mark: Cover food and refuse bins
1 mark: Dispose of refuse and faeces properly, e.g. sanitary latrines
1 mark: Use insecticides, fly traps or screens
questions.explanation: Aedes mosquitoes carry yellow fever; tsetse flies carry sleeping sickness. Houseflies are controlled by covering food and refuse, sanitary disposal and insecticides or screens.

questions.stem:
(a) Who is a quack? [2 marks]
(b) State three dangers of patronising quacks. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: A person who pretends to have medical knowledge or skills and treats people without training or licence
1 mark: Wrong diagnosis and treatment
1 mark: Use of unsafe or fake drugs leading to complications or death
1 mark: Loss of money and delay in getting proper treatment
questions.explanation: A quack claims unqualified medical skill. Patronising quacks risks misdiagnosis, harmful drugs, death, wasted money and delayed proper care.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between solid waste and liquid waste, giving two examples of each. [6 marks]
(b) Describe four methods of solid waste disposal. [8 marks]
(c) State three health hazards of indiscriminate refuse dumping. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Solid waste: discarded solid materials, e.g. food remains, paper, cans, plastics
3 marks: Liquid waste: used water and fluids, e.g. sewage, sullage from kitchens and baths, industrial effluent
2 marks: Sanitary landfill: waste spread, compacted and covered with soil
2 marks: Incineration: burning at high temperature in a furnace
2 marks: Composting: organic waste decomposed into manure
2 marks: Recycling/reuse or controlled tipping and burial
2 marks: Breeding of flies, rats and mosquitoes that spread disease
2 marks: Blockage of drains causing flooding
2 marks: Offensive odour, air pollution and contamination of water sources
questions.explanation: Solid wastes are refuse; liquid wastes are sewage and sullage. Methods include landfill, incineration, composting and recycling. Dumping breeds vectors, blocks drains, pollutes water and smells.

questions.stem:
(a) What is first aid? [2 marks]
(b) State four qualities of a good first aider. [4 marks]
(c) Describe the first aid treatment for each of the following: (i) fainting (ii) snake bite (iii) choking in an adult. [14 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Immediate care given to a sick or injured person before professional help arrives
1 mark: Calm and confident
1 mark: Observant and quick
1 mark: Tactful and sympathetic
1 mark: Knowledgeable and resourceful
2 marks: Fainting: lay casualty flat and raise the legs
2 marks: Fainting: loosen tight clothing, ensure fresh air, reassure on recovery
2 marks: Snake bite: keep casualty calm and still; immobilise the limb below heart level
2 marks: Snake bite: do not cut, suck or apply tight tourniquet; remove rings
1 mark: Snake bite: take to hospital quickly, noting the snake's appearance
2 marks: Choking: encourage coughing; give up to five firm back blows between the shoulder blades
2 marks: Choking: give up to five abdominal thrusts, alternating with back blows
1 mark: Choking: call for emergency help; begin CPR if the casualty becomes unresponsive
questions.explanation: First aid is immediate care before professional help. A good first aider is calm, observant, tactful and resourceful. Fainting: lie flat with legs raised. Snake bite: calm, immobilise, no cutting or sucking, rush to hospital. Choking: back blows and abdominal thrusts, then CPR if unresponsive.

questions.stem:
(a) Classify behaviour-altering drugs into four groups, giving one example of each. [8 marks]
(b) State six effects of drug abuse on the individual and society. [12 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Stimulants, e.g. cocaine, amphetamine, caffeine
2 marks: Depressants, e.g. alcohol, barbiturates, diazepam
2 marks: Hallucinogens, e.g. LSD, cannabis in high doses
2 marks: Narcotics/opioids, e.g. heroin, morphine, codeine, tramadol
2 marks: Damage to organs such as the brain, liver and lungs
2 marks: Addiction and mental illness
2 marks: Poor academic performance and school dropout
2 marks: Crime, violence and road accidents
2 marks: Broken homes and family conflict
2 marks: Loss of productivity and cost to the nation
questions.explanation: Drugs are stimulants, depressants, hallucinogens and narcotics. Abuse damages organs and the mind, ruins education and families, and fuels crime and accidents.

questions.stem: With reference to tuberculosis: (a) name the causative organism; [2 marks] (b) state two modes of transmission; [4 marks] (c) list four signs and symptoms; [8 marks] (d) state three methods of prevention and control. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Mycobacterium tuberculosis, a bacterium
2 marks: Inhalation of droplets from coughing or sneezing of an infected person
2 marks: Drinking unpasteurised milk from infected cattle or close contact in overcrowded rooms
2 marks: Persistent cough for more than two weeks
2 marks: Coughing up blood-stained sputum
2 marks: Night sweats and fever
2 marks: Weight loss and chest pain
2 marks: BCG immunisation
2 marks: Early detection and complete treatment (DOTS)
2 marks: Good ventilation, avoiding overcrowding and covering coughs
questions.explanation: TB is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, spread by droplets and unpasteurised milk. Symptoms include chronic cough, haemoptysis, night sweats and weight loss. Prevent with BCG, complete treatment and ventilation.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the term safe motherhood. [4 marks]
(b) State four components of safe motherhood. [8 marks]
(c) Describe four methods of family planning. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: Ensuring that women go through pregnancy, childbirth and the period after delivery safely, with healthy babies
2 marks: Antenatal care
2 marks: Skilled attendance and clean, safe delivery
2 marks: Postnatal care
2 marks: Family planning and emergency obstetric care
2 marks: Barrier methods such as condoms prevent sperm reaching the egg
2 marks: Hormonal methods such as pills, injectables and implants
2 marks: Intrauterine device placed in the uterus
2 marks: Natural methods (calendar/rhythm) or permanent methods (vasectomy, tubal ligation)
questions.explanation: Safe motherhood aims at safe pregnancy and childbirth through antenatal care, skilled delivery, postnatal care and family planning. Methods include barrier, hormonal, IUD, natural and permanent methods.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the term defence mechanism. [2 marks]
(b) Describe any four defence mechanisms with an example of each. [12 marks]
(c) State three ways of promoting mental health in a secondary school. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Unconscious ways the mind uses to protect itself from anxiety or unpleasant feelings
3 marks: Rationalisation: giving acceptable but false reasons, e.g. 'the exam was not important anyway'
3 marks: Displacement: transferring feelings to a safer target, e.g. kicking a chair after being scolded
3 marks: Regression: returning to childish behaviour, e.g. a student sulking and sucking a thumb
3 marks: Sublimation/compensation/denial/repression: correct explanation and example
2 marks: Provide guidance and counselling services
2 marks: Encourage sports, clubs and recreation
2 marks: Reduce bullying and create a supportive environment
questions.explanation: Defence mechanisms protect the self from anxiety: rationalisation, displacement, regression, sublimation and others. Schools promote mental health through counselling, recreation and anti-bullying policies.
